text_to_speech: Devi Omega: Hey guys, it is Devi here. Welcome back to our interview series: Building the Future with WAX. Today we’re sitting down with Lukas from WAX. So Lukas, for the folks at home, tell us what it is that you do at WAX. Lukas Sliwka: I’m essentially the head of engineering at WAX. I’m responsible for building out the platform, managing the team, also operations of the team and the culture. That type of stuff. Devi: And so, I mean, you obviously have a lot of people that work with you What do you guys… I mean, what’s exciting that you guys got going on right now? Lukas: Right now… Devi: What’s top of the list? Lukas:There’s a whole bunch of great stuff that we’re working on, both on the business side and technology side. I think what makes OPSkins and WAX very exciting as a place is that we are always operating in uncharted waters. So, we’re redefining the space in terms of business. Right? We’ve got very very exciting initiatives going on. But also, on the technology side, you know, we’re trying to apply blockchain to an e-commerce grade type of environment. And that’s not easy. Devi: I mean, building a business is hard enough on its own, but building a business in a completely new sort of technology sector adds just another extra layer of difficulty to something. So, it’s pretty amazing what you guys are able to do. The blockchain obviously is a very exciting technology. There’s a lot of things coming out with it, and there’s a lot of different companies out there who are trying different things. So for you, why WAX? I mean, what sort of spoke to you about the company that made you want to hop on board? Lukas: I was looking for companies that had a really good leadership behind them because that’s very important. You know, one big thing for me, and that’s something that I’m working with my team on, is this needs to be a learning environment. We all need to be learning new things, right? So I want to work for people who are, you know, breaking ground. Right? So that’s number one. Devi: And it’s a particular sort of mentality and culture that has to happen to ... Lukas: That’s exactly right. Devi: ... foster that kind of environment, and that starts with leadership. So… Lukas: That’s exactly right. And then the last thing was the technology aspect. Right? So, I’ve done many many different things over the last twenty years, and I believe that blockchain is at that point where it’s about to to take off. The technology will be used for many different things. Devi: For you, you obviously know a lot about blockchain. What do you think are the most exciting applications of the technology? Obviously WAX is one, but are there any others that sort of speak to you? Lukas: Well, yeah. I think that, you know, any time that you start dealing with decentralization and security, where you want to set up a highly transparent system with no one really, no one party owning it Devi: Yeah, no or like overruler. just shut it down right but at the end of the day Lukas: There’s no one overlord that can just kind of, that can just shut it down. But at the end of the day, this notion that we are going after, where you as an owner of like a digital item, you truly own it. Right? Devi: And that’s a huge cultural shift as well, because I mean I think a lot of people are just so used to, especially gamers, are so used to being thinking of things like. It’s a very narrow sort of trajectory where it’s like, “Oh I own this thing and I can only use it in this game”. Lukas: Right. Devi: But you don’t even really own it. It’s just this… It’s on lend to you from the lord, the overlord we were talking about. Lukas: Well, perfect example, I mean, VGO kind of took off. Right? And this is an example where you have an economy first Item-centric ecosystem first. And, you know, the bet, the bet was, you know, can you have, you know, item trading without having a game? Right? Would having a healthy trading economy spur actually gaming publishers to kind of come in like, “Hey, can we integrate these items in our game?”. Right? And that’s exactly what’s happening. Right? Devi: Yeah. Lukas: So, we’re talking to gaming companies now who are looking at VGO and they’re like: “Wow”. Like there’s a healthy economy there, right? And people are trading. It’s massive, right? And now they are going to integrate that in their games because they know that having that ecosystem of, you know, trading and the economy of the items extends the lifespan of a game. Right? Devi: Oh yeah. Definitely. Wow, aww man. Every time I sit down to do one of these interviews, it’s just, it gets me more and more and more excited about just what is coming up and what you guys got going on because it’s… There’s things we can’t even talk about it yet, which is like… Lukas: Yeah, there’s some things we can’t talk about it, but you know, some of the top secret stuff that we’re working on right now, I believe, and that’s another reason why I’m here is you know, we are going to potentially redefine ecommerce space. Devi: Alright Lukas: So, it’s going to be awesome. Devi: I can’t wait. Alright, well Lukas, thank you so much for joining us today. Devi: So, thank you guys so much for watching. We appreciate you being here with us. Make sure to head over to WAX’s social media, and as for us make sure you subscribe, like, comment, let us know what you want to see. So, thank you guys again so much. Lukas, thank you. Lukas: Thank you. Devi: Lukas and Dev, out.
